title: The Loves of Abu Isa and Kurrat al-Ayn (മലയാളം)

full_text:
Prince Abu Isa, son of the Caliph Al-Rashid, was walking through the palace gardens of his brother, Caliph Al-Ma'mun, when he heard a voice of peerless purity singing classical verses to the accompaniment of an ivory lute from behind a jasmine trellis.

The singer was Kurrat al-Ayn, a maiden of noble education and sublime artistic mastery, who was the favorite singer of Al-Ma'mun’s court. Abu Isa stood enchanted, his heart pierced by the beauty of her melody and the refined intellect expressed in her improvisation.

Rather than using his royal rank to demand her presence, Prince Abu Isa composed an elegant poetic petition in the classic meter, expressing his sincere admiration for her artistry and seeking permission to court her with honorable intentions.

Caliph Al-Ma'mun, discovering the correspondence, summoned both the prince and the maiden to the grand audience chamber. 'Abu Isa,' said the Caliph with imperial gravity, 'Kurrat al-Ayn is the pride of my court. If you wish to claim her hand, you must prove that your mind matches her artistry. She shall compose three musical verses on the theme of royal justice, and you must answer each on the spot with equal rhyme and philosophical depth.'

Kurrat al-Ayn struck her lute and sang of the balance of the scales, the defense of the weak, and the light of knowledge. Abu Isa answered each stanza with spontaneous verses of such brilliance, humility, and chivalric grace that the entire assembly applauded in delight.

Al-Ma'mun smiled with deep fraternal joy, bestowed upon them a magnificent palace on the Tigris, and celebrated a wedding that became an enduring model of courtly refinement and mutual respect.
moral: Courtly refinement, poetic eloquence, and respectful conduct win the highest favors of monarchs. [ML]
